packet.headline_seed: Suspected boat explosion injures 11 in Miami
packet.description_seed: Officials are investigating what caused the explosion at a popular marina in southern Florida.

what: Suspected boat explosion injures 11 in Miami

clean_source_blocks.text: Florida wildlife commission investigating cause of incident that left passengers with burns and traumatic injuries Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email A suspected boat explosion at a Miami sandbar sent at least 11 people to the hospital on Saturday with some suffering from burns and traumatic injuries, according to Juan Arias, the Miami Dade fire rescue battalion chief. First responders received reports roughly around 12.45pm of a possible boat explosion on the water, Arias told WPEC 12. It is unclear what caused the blast, which occurred onboard a charter boat with about 14 people, according to NBC 6 South Florida. The Florida fish and wildlife conservation commission is investigating the incident, according to the Associated Press.

At least 15 people were injured after a suspected boat explosion near a popular sandbar off the coast of Miami Beach on Saturday, emergency officials said. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue said more than 25 rescue units responded to reports of a possible vessel explosion near Haulover Sandbar at about 12:45 local time. The United States Coast Guard and the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission also assisted in the response. Emergency crews arriving at the scene found multiple people suffering from injuries, including burns and trauma wounds, according to Miami-Dade Fire Rescue Battalion Chief Juan Arias. Authorities said the number of casualties prompted officials to upgrade the incident to a Level 2 Mass Casualty Incident in order to request additional resources.

Miami-Dade Fire Rescue initially said 15 people had been transported to hospital, though later updates indicated that 11 patients were taken for further treatment. Officials did not immediately release details about the severity of the injuries. The cause of the explosion has not been confirmed and remains under investigation. A witness, local boat charter operator Robert Lee, said he saw the blast and believed it was caused by fuel ignition. “We saw three people fly out of the boat,” Lee said. “So this guy got in a hurry, and his people got on board, and he turned the key, and didn't open the hatches. Didn't turn on the blowers and he blew people out the boat.”

Lee said the vessel became engulfed in flames within minutes. “I just saw a lot of them with burns all over them,” he said. “It is quick, but it's high octane gasoline, and so a lot of them got burnt and it was an explosion.” Fire officials urged boaters to take safety precautions, particularly during the busy summer season. “This time of year, we have a lot of boats on the water, so it's always good to make sure you have a radio with you, life vests, fire extinguishers in case of fighting any fires or explosions like we had today,” Arias said. “And also have an experienced boater with you on the boat, a captain or whatnot.” Get Latest News Live on Times Now along with Breaking News and Top Headlines from US News and around the World.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
US authorities are investigating the cause of an explosion on board a boat that injured 11 people in Miami, southern Florida.

Miami-Dade Fire Rescue Battalion Chief Juan Arias told reporters that emergency crews responded to reports of a "possible boat explosion" at Haulover Sandbar, a popular tourist location.

Eleven people were taken to local hospitals to be treated for burns and traumatic injuries, Arias said.

Officials have not revealed the cause of the explosion. The BBC has approached Miami-Dad Fire and Rescue for further details.

"We saw three people fly out of the boat," eyewitness and local boat charter Patrick Lee told the BBC's US partner CBS News.

"I just saw a lot of them with burns all over them, and I said that it's a hot fire," Lee added. "It is quick, but it's high octane gasoline, and so a lot of them got burnt and it was an explosion."

Videos from the scene appear to show a helicopter landing close to the Miami marina with emergency teams carrying at least one injured person on a stretcher.

Fire and rescue teams were joined by the US coast guard and Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation in responding to the incident.

Haulover Sandbar is billed as a popular tourist marina in Miami, owing to its clear and shallow water.

payload.title: Epäilty veneen räjähdys vei 11 ihmistä sairaalaan Miamissa
payload.summary: Miamin edustalla sattunut epäilty veneen räjähdys johti laajaan pelastusoperaatioon, jossa 11 ihmistä vietiin sairaalahoitoon. Viranomaiset selvittävät yhä, mikä aiheutti palon ja räjähdyksen suositulla vesialueella.
payload.content:
Miamin edustalla Floridassa 11 ihmistä vietiin sairaalaan epäillyn veneen räjähdyksen jälkeen lauantaina. Pelastusviranomaisten mukaan osa loukkaantuneista sai palovammoja ja muita vammoja, ja onnettomuuden syytä tutkivat Floridan luonnonvara- ja kalastusviranomaiset yhdessä muiden viranomaisten kanssa.

## Pelastusyksiköitä hälytettiin laajasti

Miami-Daden pelastuslaitos sai ilmoituksen mahdollisesta veneen räjähdyksestä noin kello 12.45 paikallista aikaa. Tapaus sattui Haulover Sandbarin lähellä, joka on suosittu veneilijöiden kokoontumispaikka Miamin rannikon edustalla.

Paikalle lähetettiin yli 25 pelastusyksikköä. Myös Yhdysvaltain rannikkovartiosto ja Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission osallistuivat viranomaisten mukaan tilanteeseen. Loukkaantuneiden määrän vuoksi tapaus luokiteltiin toisen tason suuronnettomuustilanteeksi, jotta lisäresursseja saatiin nopeasti käyttöön.

Viranomaistietojen mukaan alkuvaiheessa sairaalaan kuljetettujen määräksi ilmoitettiin 15, mutta myöhemmissä päivityksissä sairaalahoitoon vietyjen määräksi tarkentui 11. Kaikkien vammojen vakavuudesta ei ollut heti yksityiskohtaista tietoa.

## Syy on yhä tutkinnassa

Räjähdyksen tarkkaa syytä ei ole vahvistettu. Viranomaisten mukaan tapaus sattui charter-veneessä, jossa oli tietojen mukaan noin 14 ihmistä. Silminnäkijä ja paikallinen venevuokraaja Robert Lee arvioi nähneensä räjähdyksen ja epäili sen liittyneen polttoaineen syttymiseen, mutta kyseessä ei ole viranomaisten vahvistama tieto.

Leen mukaan alus syttyi liekkeihin muutamassa minuutissa. Hän kertoi nähneensä useita palovammoja saaneita ihmisiä ja sanoi kolmen ihmisen sinkoutuneen ulos veneestä räjähdyksen yhteydessä. Nämä havainnot kuvaavat tilanteen vakavuutta, mutta viranomaistutkinta ratkaisee, mikä räjähdyksen lopulta aiheutti.

## Veneilijöitä muistutettiin varautumisesta

Pelastusviranomaiset muistuttivat tapauksen jälkeen veneilijöitä varautumisesta erityisesti vilkkaana veneilykautena. Miami-Daden pelastuslaitoksen edustaja Juan Arias korosti muun muassa radiopuhelimen, pelastusliivien ja palosammuttimien merkitystä sekä kokeneen veneilijän tai kapteenin mukanaoloa.

Tutkinta jatkuu, ja viranomaiset pyrkivät selvittämään, mikä johti räjähdykseen ja sitä seuranneisiin vammoihin. Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission on mukana tapauksen selvittämisessä.

Pelastusviranomaiset hälyttivät paikalle yli 25 yksikköä ja luokittelivat tilanteen suuronnettomuudeksi.
Räjähdyksen syytä ei ole vahvistettu, ja tutkinta jatkuu Floridan viranomaisten johdolla.
payload.journalist_note: Kirjoitettu vain paketissa olleiden tietojen perusteella. Loukkaantuneiden määrässä käytetty myöhempää tarkentunutta lukua 11; alkuvaiheen 15 mainitaan taustana.

Miami-Dade Fire Rescue initially said 15 people had been transported to hospital, though later updates indicated that 11 patients were taken for further treatment. Officials did not immediately release details about the severity of the injuries. The cause of the explosion has not been confirmed and remains under investigation. A witness, local boat charter operator Robert Lee, said he saw the blast and believed it was caused by fuel ignition. “We saw three people fly out of the boat,” Lee said. “So this guy got in a hurry, and his people got on board, and he turned the key, and didn't open the hatches. Didn't turn on the blowers and he blew people out the boat.”

Lee said the vessel became engulfed in flames within minutes. “I just saw a lot of them with burns all over them,” he said. “It is quick, but it's high octane gasoline, and so a lot of them got burnt and it was an explosion.” Fire officials urged boaters to take safety precautions, particularly during the busy summer season. “This time of year, we have a lot of boats on the water, so it's always good to make sure you have a radio with you, life vests, fire extinguishers in case of fighting any fires or explosions like we had today,” Arias said. “And also have an experienced boater with you on the boat, a captain or whatnot.” Get Latest News Live on Times Now along with Breaking News and Top Headlines from US News and around the World.
